_comment: Source of truth for the versions offered in the documentation version switcher.
ORDERING RULE: publish the versioned directory FIRST (workflow_dispatch of
docs-deploy.yml with source_ref set to the release tag), confirm it renders,
and only THEN add its entry here. An entry added before its directory exists
is a dropdown link that 404s -- exactly the failure mode versioned docs are
meant to prevent.
'dir' is the directory under the docs site root. It MUST match the
SPHINX_CCCL_VER used to build that version, because docs/conf.py sets
html_theme_options.switcher.version_match from that value; a mismatch leaves
the switcher unable to highlight the version the reader is currently on.
Directories are MAJOR.MINOR, matching docs/VERSION.md on the release branch.
Patch releases refresh their minor directory in place rather than adding a
new one -- see the retention note below for why per-patch directories are
not an option.
'latest_stable' names the entry aliased at /latest/ and used as the redirect
target for the site root and for legacy unversioned URLs. Keep it null until
a stable version has actually been published; while it is null the site root
redirects to unstable/, preserving today's behavior.
RETENTION: GitHub Pages refuses to publish a site larger than 1 GB. A built
CCCL version measures 130-180 MB, so the site holds roughly five directories
in total, main included. 'size_budget_versions' is the number this list is
expected to stay within; exceeding it is a warning at build time, not an
error, because the real remedy is a decision about which release to drop.
